findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0364: Exported And Unprotected Activities That Expose Sensitive Functionality
findings.explanation:
cert4android's TrustCertificateActivity is exported with no permission and records a certificate trust decision taken from the intent (EXTRA_CERTIFICATE + EXTRA_TRUSTED). Any app can start it, and on a repeat delivery (singleInstance, onNewIntent) the attacker's certificate is saved as user-trusted without a tap. User-trusted certificates bypass hostname checks, so CalDAV/Tasks.org traffic, including Basic-auth credentials, can be intercepted. Ward's analyzer said: Exported activities without a permission. Ward lists them; check whether each one exposes sensitive functionality or trusts its intent's data.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0366: Exported And Unprotected Broadcast Receivers That Expose Sensitive Functionality
findings.explanation:
PebbleService registers a context receiver for com.getpebble.action.app.RECEIVE with RECEIVER_EXPORTED and no permission, on every app start. Any installed app can send Pebble-formatted messages that complete or save tasks (MSG_COMPLETE_TASK, MSG_SAVE_TASK) and trigger task reads. Manifest receivers (FireReceiver checks for an explicit intent; system-event receivers) weren't found to act on untrusted extras. Ward's analyzer said: Exported receivers without a permission. Ward lists them; check whether each one exposes sensitive functionality or trusts its intent's data.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0339: SQL Injection in Content Providers
findings.explanation:
The exported TasksContentProvider (todoagenda URI) puts the caller's selection string straight into SQL via SupportSQLiteQueryBuilder and runs only `.sql`, dropping selectionArgs. A caller holding READ_TASKS can inject SQL (e.g. UNION SELECT) to read any table.
app/src/main/java/org/tasks/provider/TasksContentProvider.kt:60: Caller-controlled selection is concatenated into the raw SQL that rawQuery executes.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0208: Insufficient Key Sizes
findings.explanation:
The AndroidKeyStore AES key that encrypts stored account passwords is generated without setKeySize, so it gets the 128-bit default, which the test treats as insufficient.
kmp/src/androidMain/kotlin/org/tasks/security/AndroidKeyProvider.kt:27: KeyGenParameterSpec built without setKeySize(256); AES defaults to 128 bits.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0282: Unsafe Custom Trust Evaluation
findings.explanation:
The custom X509TrustManager (cert4android) trusts any certificate stored as user-trusted before checking the system store. Because the exported TrustCertificateActivity lets another app record that decision, a certificate can be trusted without real user validation.
cert4android/src/androidMain/kotlin/at/bitfire/cert4android/CustomCertStore.kt:83: User-trusted certificates are accepted before system validation.
cert4android/src/androidMain/kotlin/at/bitfire/cert4android/TrustCertificateActivity.kt:99: The trust decision can come from an external intent extra.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0283: Incorrect Implementation of Server Hostname Verification
findings.explanation:
The HostnameVerifier returns true for any hostname when the leaf certificate is in the user-trusted store, so a user-trusted (or externally injected) certificate is valid for every host.
cert4android/src/jvmCommonMain/kotlin/at/bitfire/cert4android/CustomCertManager.kt:78: Hostname mismatch is accepted when the certificate is user-trusted.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0374: References to Implicit Intents Carrying Sensitive Extras
findings.explanation:
Task titles and details are sent to the Pebble companion app through PebbleKit.sendDataToPebbleWithTransactionId, which dispatches a broadcast from library code; whether the library restricts the recipient package can't be seen in the app's sources.
kmp/src/androidMain/kotlin/org/tasks/pebble/PebbleProtocol.kt:138: Task data handed to PebbleKit's broadcast-based transport.

findings.title: MASWE-0030: Improper Use of the Clipboard
findings.explanation:
The generated Tasks.org app password is copied to the clipboard with a plain ClipData and no EXTRA_IS_SENSITIVE flag, so it appears in clipboard previews and stays readable by keyboards and clipboard managers.
app/src/main/java/org/tasks/utility/CopyToClipboard.kt:19: Clip is set without marking it sensitive.
app/src/main/java/org/tasks/preferences/fragments/TasksAccount.kt:151: Used for the password field of the new app-password dialog.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0315: Sensitive Data Exposed via Notifications
findings.explanation:
minSdk is 26 and reminder notifications show the task title and description with no lock-screen visibility (setVisibility/setPublicVersion is never used). Whether users' task content counts as sensitive is a product decision.
app/src/main/java/org/tasks/notifications/NotificationManager.kt:493: Task title is shown in the reminder notification, public on the lock screen by default.

findings.explanation:

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0231: References to Logging APIs
findings.explanation:
Release builds plant a FileLogger (Timber DebugTree, all priorities) and the Microsoft Graph client logs HTTP HEADERS in release via Timber.d. Authorization is sanitized, but Cookie/Set-Cookie headers are not; logs go to cacheDir and can be exported with logcat in a support zip. Whether those Graph cookies are session-sensitive needs a human decision.
app/src/main/java/org/tasks/http/HttpClientFactory.kt:64: Release builds log request/response headers of the Graph client; only Authorization is sanitized.
